# Intake Brief — Add compaction fallback model chain (OpenRouter → Muse → local Qwen3)

**Work Item:** LP-0MTSDDD4E004DNF0
**Parent:** LP-0MTPK77WG009A4VH — Investigate Muse compaction hang via Responses API translation layer
**Type:** feature
**Priority:** medium

**Headline:** Add a three-tier cascading fallback chain for proxy-side session compaction summarization (OpenRouter free → Muse on OpenCode → local Qwen3) so compaction continues reliably even when the local model is unavailable.

## Problem Statement

The proxy-side session compaction summarizer currently supports only a single local model (Qwen3 via llama-server). When the local model is unavailable or under heavy GPU contention, compaction silently falls through to non-compactable sessions. A cascading fallback chain — OpenRouter free tier → Muse on OpenCode → local Qwen3 — would significantly improve compaction reliability.

## Users

- **Proxy operators** — need compaction to work reliably regardless of local GPU availability, without additional infrastructure
- **Pi users** — benefit from compacted sessions maintaining fast response times across long conversations

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Config defines a three-tier fallback chain:** The proxy config includes a `summarizer_model` section with a cascading fallback chain: OpenRouter (`google/gemma-4-31b-it:free`) → Muse on OpenCode (`muse-spark-1.2-contributor`) → local Qwen3.
2. **AC2 — OpenRouter primary summarizer works:** When configured with a valid `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` env var, the summarizer calls OpenRouter's `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` as the model, using the same summarizer prompt and response parsing as the local summarizer.
3. **AC3 — Cascading fallback on failure:** If the OpenRouter call fails (HTTP error, timeout, or empty response), the summarizer transparently retries with Muse via the existing OpenCode remote provider configuration. If Muse also fails, it falls back to the local Qwen3 summarizer.
4. **AC4 — Fail-open behavior preserved:** The summarizer returns empty string on any failure at any tier (never blocks dispatch). Each fallback transition is logged at WARNING level with the failure reason.
5. **AC5 — Existing local-only behavior unchanged when config omits remote tiers:** If `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is not set or the config does not specify a remote summarizer, the system falls back directly to local Qwen3 (the current behavior).

## Constraints

- **No new infrastructure dependencies** — must use existing proxy remote-call infrastructure (httpx for OpenRouter, existing OpenCode provider config for Muse).
- **Must not break existing compaction** — all existing local-only summarizer behavior must be preserved as the final fallback.
- **Timeout must be bounded** — each tier has a configurable timeout (default 30s) so compaction never stalls.
- **Config change is additive** — existing `summarizer_model: {type: local, llama_model: Qwen3}` config should continue to work (local-only path).

## Existing State

- **Current summarizer:** Single local model — `proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` builds a `Summarizer` callable backed by `llama-server` on port 8080, using `summarizer_model.llama_model` from config.
- **Config structure:** `server.summarizer_model` in `config.yaml` — currently only supports `{type: local, llama_model: Qwen3}`.
- **Compaction wiring:** `router_helpers.py:_evaluate_session_compaction` receives the summarizer callable and passes it to `decide_session_compaction`.
- **OpenRouter in proxy:** No OpenRouter provider currently configured in `config.yaml`. OpenRouter model IDs exist in `provider_resolver.py` mapping tables but are not used as remote providers.
- **OpenCode Muse:** Configured in `plan`, `author`, `code` model providers as `muse-spark-1.2-contributor` via `opencode-go` provider with `api: openai-responses`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/config.yaml` — Add `summarizer_model` with remote + local fallback entries
- `proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` — Extend `build_local_summarizer` (or create `build_fallback_summarizer`) to support multi-tier dispatch
- `proxy/provider.py` — Update `compaction_config()` to parse the new fallback chain structure
- `proxy/router_helpers.py` — Update call site to use the new fallback summarizer builder

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: OpenRouter rate limits** — The free model tier on OpenRouter may have aggressive rate limits that cause compaction timeouts. Mitigation: bounded timeouts + automatic fallback to next tier.
- **Risk: OpenRouter API key availability** — Requires `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` env var to be set. If absent, system must gracefully skip OpenRouter tier and fall through to local. This is handled by the "existing local-only behavior unchanged" constraint.
- **Risk: Compaction latency increase** — Three-tier fallback could increase worst-case compaction latency. Mitigation: each tier has a bounded timeout (default 30s); overall timeout cap.
- **Scope creep: full multi-model routing** — This change is scoped to compaction summarization only. Do not expand to other model routing paths (plan/author/code) without separate work items.
- **Assumption: OpenRouter /v1/chat/completions endpoint format** — OpenRouter is OpenAI-compatible, so the same request/response format as the local llama-server should work.
- **Assumption: Muse via OpenCode supports the summarizer prompt format** — Muse is already used as a fallback in plan/author/code providers, so it should work.

## Related Work

- **LP-0MTPK77WG009A4VH** — Investigate Muse compaction hang via Responses API translation layer (parent)
- **LP-0MTPMJG1P0038D32** — Implement proxy-side summarizer backed by local Qwen3 (completed)
- **LP-0MTPMJGC3007YG0S** — Wire the summarizer + routing estimator into _evaluate_session_compaction (in review)
- **LP-0MTPMEQ5V005CMZ7** — Evaluate OpenRouter free models for proxy-side summarization (evaluation; this item supersedes with implementation)

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What is the fallback chain?" — Answer (user): "google/gemma-4-31b-it:free via OpenRouter → muse on opencode → local Qwen3". Source: user request.
- Q: "Should this replace the existing local summarizer or be additive?" — Answer (inferred from spec): Additive — the existing local Qwen3 is the final fallback tier. Source: user said "falling back to muse on opencode, falling back to the local Qwen model."

# Problem Statement

The proxy usage report tracks session duration (Time to Completion) and decode/prompt-eval speed, but does **not** track time to first token (TTFT) — the latency from request dispatch to the first token emitted. This is a key user-experience metric for both local (llama-server prefill + first token) and remote provider latency, and it's currently invisible in the daily usage report.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **Proxy-side TTFT logging:**
   - [ ] Remote stream path (proxy_remote.py) emits a structured log line with TTFT measurement (time from request start to first actual data chunk), formatted as `ttft_seconds=<float> session=<id> provider=<provider> model=<model>`.
   - [ ] The existing `dispatch_first_byte_ms` log in the local stream path (router.py) is preserved — this is TTFT for local streams.
   - [ ] Only streaming responses (SSE) are measured; non-streaming requests are unchanged.

2. **Report section:**
   - [ ] A new `## Time to first token` section is added to the usage report, placed **before** the existing `## Time to completion` section.
   - [ ] The section parses TTFT data from both log sources: `dispatch_first_byte_ms=` lines (local) and `ttft_seconds=` lines (remote).
   - [ ] A table displays **Median**, **p10**, and **p90** columns (matching the existing "Time to completion" table style) with **Total**, **Fast**, and **Cheap** columns.
   - [ ] When no TTFT data is available in the window, the section shows "_No TTFT data in window._".
   - [ ] The JSON `--json` output includes a `ttft` field with the same percentile data.

3. **Testing:**
   - [ ] Unit tests for the new log line parsers (both local `dispatch_first_byte_ms` and remote `ttft_seconds`).
   - [ ] Unit tests for the report section rendering (including empty-data case).
   - [ ] Full test suite passes.

# Constraints

- The local path already has `dispatch_first_byte_ms` logged — this **is** TTFT for local streams. Do not duplicate or change this logging.
- The remote path needs new TTFT logging added with minimal surgical changes to `proxy_remote.py`.
- TTFT is measured from dispatch (remote: HTTP request send time) to the first data chunk.
- Remote TTFT includes network latency to the provider — this is a known limitation and will be documented in the report.
- Fast/Cheap bucketing follows the existing mode-aware logic.
- The remote log line uses `ttft_seconds` (seconds, not ms) to avoid confusion with the existing local `dispatch_first_byte_ms` metric.

# Existing State

- **Local path (router.py):** Captures `_dispatch_start = time.monotonic()` and emits `dispatch_first_byte_ms=%.1f dispatch_to_first_byte_ms=%.1f session=%s model=%s` when the first data chunk arrives. This is TTFT for local streams.
- **Remote path (proxy_remote.py):** No TTFT logging. The first data chunk detection already exists (the `_first_byte_emitted` / `_has_actual_data` pattern), but no timestamp is captured at dispatch time.
- **Report (reporting.py):** `_append_ttc_section` renders "Time to completion" with p10/median/p90 for session duration. No TTFT section exists.
- **Log parser (log_parser.py):** No regex for `dispatch_first_byte_ms` or `ttft_seconds`.

# Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — Local stream path; TTFT already logged, no changes needed.
- `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py` — Remote stream path; needs TTFT start timestamp and log emission.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — Needs regex to parse `dispatch_first_byte_ms` and `ttft_seconds` log lines.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — May need to expose TTFT data to the report.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — New `_append_ttft_section` function, placed before `_append_ttc_section`.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — Tests for the new parsing and reporting.

- **LP-0MTJET616005S7PN:** Dispatch→first-byte capture — the existing local TTFT logging.

# Intake Brief — Add "compact" model (Muse → DeepSeek) and wire proxy-side compaction to it

## Problem Statement
Proxy-side session compaction currently calls the local llama-server directly (`localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions` with Qwen3). Under load all 3 slots are saturated, causing every summarizer call to time out (49/49 timeouts observed at 30s). A remote fallback model is needed that does not contend with local GPU slots. The new `compact` model should use Muse (via opencode-go) as primary and DeepSeek (`deepseek-v4-flash` via `api.deepseek.com`) as fallback, and the compaction summarizer must use this model instead of the direct local call.

## Users
- **Proxy operators** — need compaction to succeed without local GPU contention; no extra llama-server required.
- **Pi users** — benefit from compacted sessions maintaining fast routing (fast ≤38K / cheap ≤30K targets) across long conversations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — Config defines `models.compact` fallback chain:** `proxy/config.yaml` adds a `compact:` entry under `models:` with two providers in order: (1) Muse (`muse-spark-1.2-contributor` via `opencode-go` provider, `https://opencode.ai/zen/go`, same as `plan`/`author`/`code`), (2) DeepSeek (`deepseek-v4-flash` via `deepseek` provider `https://api.deepseek.com` with `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`). Mirrors existing provider definitions (including `forward_session_headers: false`, `api: openai-responses` for Muse where needed). No `local-qwen3` tier in this model — strictly remote.
- **AC2 — Compaction uses the `compact` model:** `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` (or a new `build_compact_summarizer`) routes summarization through the `compact` model via the proxy's remote-call path (not `localhost:8080`). Falls back transparently from Muse to DeepSeek on HTTP error / timeout / empty response. If both remote tiers fail, returns `""` fail-open (never blocks dispatch). Each fallback transition logged at WARNING with reason.
- **AC3 — Existing `summarizer_model` config shape preserved or migrated:** If `server.summarizer_model` previously selected `Qwen3`, the new path either (a) ignores it for `compact` (compact model owns its provider config) or (b) documents the migration — no breakage for operators who had `summarizer_model: {type: local, llama_model: Qwen3}`.
- **AC4 — Timeout is bounded:** Each tier respects `compaction_summarizer_timeout` (now 120s, see sibling item) or per-tier timeout; overall call never stalls compaction beyond the configured bound.
- **AC5 — No new infrastructure:** Uses existing proxy remote infrastructure (`httpx` / `provider_resolver` / `opencode-go` config). No second llama-server required.

## Constraints
- Must reuse existing remote provider plumbing (same env vars `OPENCODE_API_KEY` / `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` or `OPENCODE_2_API_KEY` etc. as `plan` model).
- Fail-open: any failure at any tier returns `""` so `plan_session_compaction` still produces `action=compact` with empty summary rather than blocking.
- Must not break existing compaction wiring (`router_helpers._evaluate_session_compaction` → `decide_session_compaction`).

## Existing State

# Intake Brief — Fix compaction logging: pass srv.logger so compaction_event reaches proxy.log + console

## Problem Statement
Compaction advisory events are invisible in production. `proxy/proxy/compaction.py:45` uses `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` (i.e. `proxy.compaction`), which propagates to the root logger. The app configures handlers ONLY on the `llama-proxy` logger (`setup_logging` in `utils.py`, `TimedRotatingFileHandler` → `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` + `ContentOnlyConsoleHandler`). Root has no handlers, so INFO-level `compaction_event` records are silently dropped (Python `lastResort` only handles WARNING+ on stderr). WARNING-level compaction lines leak to stderr **without** the `KeyValueFormatter` timestamp/level prefix. Result: `grep compaction_event /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` returns nothing even though the decision machinery fires on every over-trigger session.

## Users
- **Proxy operators** — need `compaction_event` lines (with `session`, `action`, `pre_tokens`, `post_tokens`, `dry_run`) in the rotated proxy.log with proper formatting to monitor compaction and prove the AC8 dry-run gate.
- **Pi users** — indirect: observable compaction enables operators to flip off dry-run safely.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — logger_obj threaded through the whole chain:** `_evaluate_session_compaction` (router_helpers.py) passes `srv.logger` (the configured `llama-proxy` logger) into `decide_session_compaction(..., logger_obj=...)` so `log_compaction_event`, `run_dry_run_plan`, and churn logging emit on the configured logger. The `_handle_session` compaction block also passes `logger_obj=srv.logger` where it calls `_evaluate_session_compaction` (if not already flowing via signature default).
- **AC2 — Events visible in proxy.log + console:** A dry-run `compaction_event` (action=compact) appears as a formatted INFO line in `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` and the console, e.g. `compaction_event session=… mode=… action=compact reason=… pre_tokens=… post_tokens=… dry_run=True`. WARNING variants (`remote_with_guidance`, backstop) appear at WARNING with the same format.
- **AC3 — No behaviour change for decisions:** Pure logging change — `action`/`messages`/`applied` semantics of `decide_session_compaction` are untouched. Existing tests asserting return values stay green.
- **AC4 — Test:** A test asserts the logger received the `compaction_event` line (mock `logger_obj` or capture via `caplog` on the passed logger) when dry-run plans an over-trigger session with a stub summarizer.

## Constraints
- Prefer passing `srv.logger` (llama-proxy) over re-pointing module loggers; module-level `logger` fallback stays for non-server contexts (e.g. CLI experiment scripts) — they can keep root-level behavior.
- No change to `logging` levels or formats elsewhere.

## Existing State
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py:45` — `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`.
- `router_helpers.py` — `_evaluate_session_compaction(srv, …)` builds config from `srv.config` and calls `decide_session_compaction` (signature accepts `logger_obj=None`); neither call site passes `logger_obj`.
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py:645 setup_logging` — configures `llama-proxy` with file + console handlers only.
- Evidence: zero `compaction_event` lines in `/tmp/proxy-startup.log` and `proxy.log` despite 49 summarizer invocations; `context_pressure` WARNINGs from `llama-proxy.provider` DO appear formatted — proving only loggers under `llama-proxy` reach the file.

- **LP-0MTPMJGC3007YG0S** — Summarizer wiring (introduced the call site).

# Intake Brief: Avoid promoting thinking to content for empty responses (LP-0MTTSBT0R004HC6B)

## Headline

Stop synthesizing thinking text (or the "Thinking..." placeholder) into `assistant.content` when the model returns only `reasoning_content`, so Pi renders thinking in its dim thinking channel rather than as bold content, while still avoiding empty-response errors.

---

## Problem Statement

When an upstream model returns empty `content` with only `reasoning_content` (thinking), the proxy currently synthesizes a value into `content` to avoid an empty-response error — originally by copying the full thinking text, now (LP-0MSEHOE7B005DE08) by emitting the hard-coded placeholder `"Thinking..."`. In both cases Pi renders the synthesized value as regular assistant **content** (bold), not as thinking (dim), so users see thinking where they expect an answer — or see a vacuous "Thinking..." bubble — even though the full thinking is already preserved untouched in `reasoning_content`.

The synthesis exists to prevent the proxy's empty-response detection (`_is_empty_response` / fallback chain) from treating thinking-only turns as failures. We need an alternative that preserves thinking, avoids the error, and keeps Pi's content/thinking rendering distinct.

## Users

- **Pi users / operators** — see thinking rendered as regular content and find the transcript confusing; long sessions also risk context bloat if thinking is replayed as content.
- **Proxy maintainers** — need a clear contract for what counts as "non-empty" when only thinking is present, without coupling content synthesis to error avoidance.

### User Stories

- *As a* Pi user, *when* the model returns only thinking, *I want* to see that thinking in Pi's dim thinking channel (and not as a bold content bubble), *so that* I can distinguish what the model thought from what it said.
- *As an* operator, *I want* thinking-only turns to not inflate session history via synthesized content, *so that* long multi-turn sessions stay within context limits.
- *As a* proxy maintainer, *I want* thinking-only turns to not trigger empty-response retry/fallback unless they truly are empty, *so that* we don't synthesize content just to satisfy an emptiness check.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No content synthesis for thinking-only turns:** When `content` is empty/null and `reasoning_content` is present without an embedded tool call, neither `_extract_assistant_content` (non-streaming) nor `_extract_assistant_content_from_sse` (streaming) copies the thinking text into `content` nor emits a placeholder that Pi renders as content. The thinking remains only in `reasoning_content`.
2. **Thinking preserved:** Session history (`proxy/proxy/session.py:extract_streamed_assistant_message_from_sse` and non-streaming persistence) continues to store the full `reasoning_content` unchanged; no thinking is dropped.
3. **No spurious empty-response errors:** A thinking-only response is **not** classified as an empty response for retry/fallback purposes. `_is_empty_response` (and the provider fallback path including `_resolve_reasoning_content_promotion` in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`) treats presence of non-empty `reasoning_content` (without tool call) as non-empty without requiring synthesized content.
4. **Tool-call extraction intact:** When `reasoning_content` contains an embedded tool call (`<function=...>...</function>`), that tool call is still extracted and returned as content-equivalent (preserving LP-0MQ6E0I06004A9G7 / LP-0MS8XAPXT009W3CL behavior).
5. **Content-preferred when present:** When real `content` exists, it is returned as-is; the new non-synthesis path only applies to the empty-content fallback.
6. **Pi rendering verified:** A manual/automated check confirms Pi displays thinking-only turns in its thinking (dim) channel and does not show a "Thinking..." or copied-thinking content bubble.
7. **Tests updated & passing:** `proxy/tests/test_incremental_ingestion.py` promotion/placeholder assertions are revised to assert the new behaviour (thinking-only → `None`/empty content, non-empty per AC3), and any other affected tests (e.g. `test_session_manager.py`) are updated. A dedicated test asserts that thinking-only is not considered empty.
8. **Documentation updated:** `proxy/README.md` and code comments in `proxy/proxy/utils.py` / `proxy/proxy/provider.py` reflect that thinking is preserved in `reasoning_content` only and not synthesized into content.
9. **Full project test suite passes.**

---

## Constraints

- Must not regress tool-call extraction from `reasoning_content` (LP-0MQ6E0I06004A9G7, LP-0MS8XAPXT009W3CL).
- Must not regress thinking-mode round-trip repairs (LP-0MSGU3JNU0092AFQ / LP-0MSCGTYWA006NAZC) or remote 400 sanitizer handling.
- Must not reintroduce context bloat from replaying thinking as content in session history.
- Alternatives must keep a single unambiguous signal for "non-empty" so the fallback chain does not oscillate between promoted-success and cooldown.
- If content is left empty, the solution must still satisfy any OpenAI-compatible schema validation that consumers (Pi, provider) apply (e.g. `content: ""` vs `content: null` vs omission).

## Existing State

- `proxy/proxy/utils.py`:
  - `_extract_assistant_content` — when `content` empty, extracts tool call from `reasoning_content` or returns `"Thinking..."` placeholder (LP-0MSEHOE7B005DE08).
  - `_extract_assistant_content_from_sse` — same placeholder fallback for streaming.
  - `_is_empty_response` — delegates to `_extract_assistant_content`; the placeholder makes thinking-only count as non-empty.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:_resolve_reasoning_content_promotion` — fallback-chain safety net that treats raw bodies containing `reasoning_content` as promoted successes; post-placeholder it is rarely reached because `_is_empty_response` is already non-empty.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py:extract_streamed_assistant_message_from_sse` — persists both `content` and `reasoning_content`; history already stores thinking untouched.
- `proxy/tests/test_incremental_ingestion.py` — asserts placeholder behaviour (`test_extract_assistant_content_*_reasoning_no_tool_call` → `"Thinking..."`) and `_is_empty_response` non-empty for thinking-only.
- Pi/TUI — `reasoning_content` rendered dim (`\033[2m`), `content` rendered bold (`\033[1m`); promotion causes thinking to appear as bold content.

## Desired Change

Evaluate and implement an alternative to content synthesis that satisfies "preserve thinking but not confuse Pi output". Preferred direction (to be confirmed via clarifying Q&A) is **stop synthesizing into `content` and make emptiness checks reasoning-aware**:

1. **Revise content extraction** in `proxy/proxy/utils.py`:
   - `_extract_assistant_content` and `_extract_assistant_content_from_sse`: when only plain thinking is present (no tool call), return `None` / empty (no placeholder, no promotion) instead of `"Thinking..."`.
   - Keep tool-call extraction branch unchanged.
2. **Revise emptiness semantics** so thinking-only is not considered empty without synthesis:
   - `_is_empty_response` (and any provider-level empty check) returns `False` when `reasoning_content` is non-empty whitespace-trimmed, even when extracted content is `None`.
   - Alternatively, centralise this in a helper like `_has_meaningful_reasoning_content` to avoid duplicating the check.
3. **Align fallback chain** in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`:
   - Ensure `_resolve_reasoning_content_promotion` or its caller treats thinking-only success consistently (thinking-only → success, not cooldown/fallback) without requiring synthesized content.
4. **Ensure schema compliance** for the empty-content case: decide whether to persist/forward `content` as `""`, `null`, or omit the key, based on what downstream validation actually requires (see Q1/Q2); document the choice.
5. **Update tests & docs**: revise `proxy/tests/test_incremental_ingestion.py` and `proxy/tests/test_session_manager.py` to assert `None`/empty content + non-empty verdict; update `proxy/README.md` and inline comments to describe "thinking stays in `reasoning_content`" contract.

**Alternatives explicitly considered but not default** (record decision in Appendix if a different path is chosen):
- **B — Sentinel placeholder with Pi-aware rendering:** keep a placeholder but make Pi render it in the thinking channel (requires Pi change; couples proxy sentinel to client).
- **C — Explicit marker string** like `"[thinking preserved — see reasoning]"` in content — still content-channel noise, not preferred.
- **D — Omit thinking from non-tool turns entirely** — violates "preserve thinking" requirement.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/utils.py` — `_extract_assistant_content`, `_extract_assistant_content_from_sse`, `_is_empty_response`, `_extract_tool_call_from_reasoning`: remove placeholder synthesis, make emptiness reasoning-aware.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_resolve_reasoning_content_promotion` and the empty-response fallback path: keep thinking-only as success without synthesized content.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `extract_streamed_assistant_message_from_sse` / persistence: verify history still stores `reasoning_content` untouched and handles empty `content`.
- `proxy/tests/test_incremental_ingestion.py` — promotion/placeholder tests, `_is_empty_response` tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_session_manager.py` — session history preservation tests for thinking-only streams.
- `proxy/README.md` — document the new contract (thinking preserved only in `reasoning_content`).

## Related Work

- **LP-0MSEHOE7B005DE08** — "promoting thinking to content" — introduced the `"Thinking..."` placeholder to fix context bloat from copying thinking verbatim; this item revisits that synthesis because the placeholder still renders as content in Pi.
- **LP-0MQP3Q8DN0047J1H** — "Fix reasoning_content-only responses (Qwen3): ensure assistant.content populated and preserve tool-call semantics" — original promotion (copy thinking into content) that LP-0MSEHOE7B005DE08 trimmed to a placeholder.
- **LP-0MQ6E0I06004A9G7** — "Fix empty content when model generates tool calls in reasoning_content" — tool-call extraction that must be preserved.
- **LP-0MS8XAPXT009W3CL** — "deepseek-v4 tool calls fail: proxy misclassifies tool-call-only streams as empty responses" — related empty-classification edge case.
- **LP-0MSGU3JNU0092AFQ / LP-0MSCGTYWA006NAZC** — thinking-mode round-trip repairs (reasoning_content 400) — must not regress.
- **LP-0MQ04EEFP006DXU9** — Pi streaming console output formatting (dim thinking vs bold content) — explains why synthesis confuses output.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk — Empty content triggers validation/400 downstream if we leave it empty.** Some consumers or schema validators may reject `content: null`/omitted when no tool calls are present. Mitigation: confirm via Q1/Q2 what error synthesis actually guards, and choose `""` vs `null` vs omission accordingly; cover with a test that exercises downstream validation.
- **Risk — Fallback/retry semantics change.** Treating thinking-only as non-empty without synthesized content shifts the condition under which the provider fallback chain is entered. Mitigation: align `_is_empty_response` and `_resolve_reasoning_content_promotion` in one place and add explicit tests for thinking-only non-empty.
- **Risk — Pi renders empty content as blank bubble.** If Pi shows nothing when both content is empty and thinking is only in `reasoning_content`, users may see a blank turn instead of "Thinking..." placeholder. Mitigation: verify Pi's existing dim rendering of `reasoning_content` already makes thinking visible without content (Q3); if not, add a Pi-side display for reasoning_content on empty-content turns — out of scope for this item but track as follow-up.
- **Assumption:** Synthesis exists solely to satisfy proxy-side emptiness detection, not an external API schema that mandates non-empty `content` on every assistant turn. If an external schema does mandate it, the fix becomes schema-specific (e.g. `content: ""` allowed).
- **Assumption:** Full thinking text can safely stay in `reasoning_content` in session history without being replayed verbatim as content; context cost is already bounded because reasoning_content is retained but not promoted.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Pi-side rendering changes, metrics, or config-gated promotion modes are out of scope; track as separate items.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1:** What specific error does synthesizing thinking into content guard against? (proxy empty-response retry/fallback, OpenAI schema 400, or Pi crash on empty content?) — *Status: OPEN QUESTION.* Evidence: `proxy/proxy/utils.py:_is_empty_response` uses synthesized content to mark thinking-only as non-empty; `_resolve_reasoning_content_promotion` is the fallback safety net. Need producer confirmation which error path is critical.
- **Q2:** Is it acceptable to leave `assistant.content` empty/null (or `""`) when thinking is present, or does any downstream consumer require non-empty `content` even when `reasoning_content` carries the thinking? Which schema value (`""` vs `null` vs omission) is allowed? — *Status: OPEN QUESTION.*
- **Q3:** Does Pi already render `reasoning_content` visibly (dim) when `content` is empty, so a thinking-only turn would still be visible to the user without any synthesized content bubble? — *Status: OPEN QUESTION.* Context: `LP-0MQ04EEFP006DXU9` confirms dim thinking vs bold content in streaming console, but need confirmation for the persisted-message / non-streaming render path.

*Interview note: No producer answers yet — brief drafted from repository exploration (proxy/proxy/utils.py, proxy/proxy/provider.py, proxy/proxy/session.py, proxy/tests/test_incremental_ingestion.py) and prior items LP-0MSEHOE7B005DE08 / LP-0MQP3Q8DN0047J1H / LP-0MQ6E0I06004A9G7. Appendix will be updated idempotently when answers arrive.*

# Intake Brief — Unknown errors from Muse (LP-0MTV77DAT0018ZUS)

**Work Item:** LP-0MTV77DAT0018ZUS
**Type:** bug
**Priority:** critical

**Headline:** Muse (opencode.ai/zen/go) upstream frequently stalls mid-stream (240s idle), emitting `stall_after_content` / `stall_exhausted` errors that neither Pi nor the proxy recovers automatically — operator must type `continue` to retry, after which the same stall often recurs.

## Problem Statement

Sessions routed to `muse-spark-1.2-contributor` via `opencode-go` (endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go`, Responses API translation) experience frequent upstream stalls. The proxy retries pre-content stalls up to 3× with backoff (2/4/8s), but **after any content has been delivered** (`stall_after_content`, 240s idle) it terminates the stream with a synthetic error chunk (`error_type: stall_after_content`, `suggested_action: "Retry the request with full context, or route to a healthier provider"`) and does **not** automatically re-dispatch to a sibling/DeepSeek provider. The client (Pi / herdr) surfaces this as a hard error requiring manual `continue`. ## Problem Statement

The local Qwen3 summarizer (backed by llama-server) times out after 30 seconds, especially under saturated slot conditions. After 3 retry attempts, the summarizer returns empty strings (fail-open), causing compaction to proceed with zero summary tokens — effectively losing conversation context.

## Users

- **Proxy operators:** Compaction is meant to keep session context bounded without losing critical information. Empty summaries defeat this purpose.
- **Session consumers (herdr agents):** Receive degraded context after compaction when summaries are empty.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Summarizer timeout increased to 120s:** The default `timeout_seconds` in `build_local_summarizer()` is raised from 30s to 120s, coordinated with LP-0MTT0PB6J0053BPP. The httpx timeout on the local summarizer POST matches this value.
2. **AC2 — Timeout errors logged with diagnostic context:** When a summarizer call times out, the warning log includes the model name, payload token count, current slot saturation, and retry attempt number to aid future debugging.
3. **AC3 — No regression in fail-open behavior:** Transport/HTTP errors still result in empty-string returns (compaction never blocks), but the warning log clearly distinguishes "timed out — try increasing timeout" from permanent failures (auth errors, model-not-found).
4. **AC4 — Compaction with empty summary is observable:** When compaction proceeds with `summary_tokens=0` due to summarizer failure, a structured log event is emitted at WARNING level that includes session ID, token counts pre/post, and the failure reason, enabling operators to detect and act on degraded compaction.
5. **AC5 — All existing proxy tests pass:** No regression in the compaction test suite or broader proxy tests.

## Constraints

- Must not change the fail-open contract — compaction must never block dispatch on summarizer errors.
- Timeout increase must not introduce unbounded latency for non-saturated scenarios (120s is a hard cap, not a soft suggestion).
- Changes are scoped to the local summarizer path; the fallback model chain (LP-0MTSDDD4E004DNF0) is a separate concern.

## Existing State

- `proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` line 265: default `timeout_seconds=30.0`

- The open item LP-0MTT0PB6J0053BPP proposes raising the timeout to 120s but is still at stage `idea`.

## Key Files (predicted)

This is the follow-up refinement to the simple per-model failure-domain fix. Always scoping by model can waste time when the gateway itself is unreachable: every model entry may be tried with retries/backoff against a dead endpoint before moving to another gateway.

## Scope: hierarchical solution

Refine failure exclusion by error class:

- Connection-level failures indicating the gateway itself is unreachable (`ConnectError`, `ConnectTimeout`, DNS failures, refused/unreachable gateway): exclude the whole endpoint failure domain.
- Request-level failures after reaching the gateway (`ReadTimeout` after connection established, HTTP 5xx, `finish_reason:error`, empty/zero-content responses, and similar model/route-level failures): exclude only the endpoint-plus-model scope.
- Keep usage-limit quarantine per API-key account, unchanged.
- Make the sibling-fallback circuit breaker and brand/entry cooldown checks consistent with the hierarchical scope.

Likely touch points in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`:

- `_failure_domain_key()` model scoping from the predecessor item
- failure classification for connection-level versus request-level errors
- `attempted_domains` call sites in fallback cycles
- `_record_sibling_failure()` / `_entry_cooldown_key()`
- tests in `tests/test_failure_domain_grouping.py` plus new hierarchical error-class cases.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

1. A connection-level gateway failure excludes all entries on that endpoint for the remainder of the request, regardless of upstream model.
2. A request-level failure for model A on a reachable gateway excludes only endpoint-plus-model A; an entry for model B on the same gateway remains eligible.
3. The fallback matrix is covered by tests: connection error versus stall/HTTP 5xx versus empty response versus usage-limit behavior across same-gateway same-model, same-gateway different-model, and different-gateway entries.
4. Sibling/brand quarantine behavior matches the hierarchical scope and does not over-quarantine healthy models after a model-specific failure.
5. Usage-limit quarantine remains account-scoped and unaffected.
6. Relevant proxy test suites pass, including updated failure-domain grouping tests.

As a proxy operator, I want a single empty-response to not poison the whole failure domain, so that sibling API keys on the same endpoint (which have independent usage limits) are still tried before falling through to another gateway.

## Goal / user story

As a proxy operator, I want the proxy to have a single, coherent path for detecting and handling oversized sessions — not three separate advisory-only signals that warn but never act. Flipping `compaction_dry_run` to `false` alone must produce working compaction, not a silent no-op or a session-invalidation loop.

## Context / evidence

The proxy has three separate code paths for the same problem (session context growing too large):

### Path 1 — Advisory warning (provider.py:629)
- Fires at `context_pressure_warn_ratio = 0.8`
- Logs a `context_pressure` WARNING with a recommendation
- Takes **zero action** — just noise

### Path 2 — Hard gate (router.py:795, provider.py:1194)
- Fires when `estimated_tokens > cap`
- Returns HTTP 429 compaction gate to the client
- **Disabled**: `local_hard_routing_cap_ratio_cheap: 0`
- Returns cap=0, so `check_hard_routing_cap()` always returns `False`

### Path 3 — Proxy-side compaction (compaction.py)
- Fires at `compaction_trigger_ratio = 0.70`
- `compaction_dry_run: true` → logs, doesn't actually compact

### Live evidence
From the proxy log snapshot (Aug 26, ~6 hours):
- **812** `context_pressure` warnings across **11 distinct sessions**
- Ratio range: 0.80 → 7.82 (sessions at up to 7.8× their per-slot context)
- **Zero compaction gates fired, zero proxy-side compactures executed**

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `should_warn_context_pressure()`, `_build_compaction_gate_response()`, `compute_hard_routing_cap()`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `check_hard_routing_cap()` gate call, `_handle_session` result consumption, `_build_session_headers()`, session persistence (`update_messages`)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_evaluate_session_compaction()`, dispatch swap (`body_override`), `compaction_applied` / `compaction_remote_with_guidance` flags
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py` — `decide_session_compaction()`, `is_compaction_dry_run()`, `plan_session_compaction()`
- `proxy/proxy/session_manager.py` — `compute_delta()` (prefix-match sync protocol)
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_classify_delta_routing()`, `merge_session_history_for_update()`, `_invalidate_session_and_slot()`
- `proxy/proxy/config.yaml` (and `config-cheap.yaml`, `config-fast.yaml`) — the three config knobs

## Root cause

Three separate paths, three separate config knobs, none with enforcement. And even the live path (Path 3 with `dry_run: false`) would not work end-to-end:

1. **`compaction_remote_with_guidance` is write-only** — set at `router_helpers.py:2183`, read by nothing. Non-compactable sessions still dispatch local near-full-slot.
2. **Client/session sync break** — after a live compaction the session store holds compacted history but the client still holds full history. The next request prefix-mismatches in `compute_delta()`, is classified `history_mismatch`, and `_invalidate_session_and_slot()` wipes the session — undoing the compaction and dropping the KV cache.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

1. `compaction_remote_with_guidance` is enforced: non-compactable oversized sessions route remote with guidance, never local near-full-slot.
2. A live compaction (`dry_run: false`) survives the next request: the session is NOT invalidated with `history_mismatch`; the compacted history persists and the delta protocol heals.
3. Only one detection knob remains (`compaction_trigger_ratio`); `context_pressure_warn_ratio` and `local_hard_routing_cap_ratio_cheap` are removed or reconciled.
4. Existing test suites pass; new tests cover guidance enforcement, post-compaction sync, and the unified trigger.

## Fix plan (in order)

### Part 1 — Enforce `remote_with_guidance` (small, ship first)
In `router.py` after `_handle_session`, check `session_result.get("compaction_remote_with_guidance")` and skip local dispatch — route remote with the `context_pressure` guidance injected. No protocol change, no client cooperation needed. Immediate slot savings for sessions that cannot be compacted.

### Part 2 — Heal the client/session sync (server-only)
Two options; Option B is implementable without client changes:
- **Option A (correct, needs client work):** add `X-Session-Compacted: true` (+ message count) response headers; the client discards its local history and re-syncs from the server. Next request prefix-matches. Requires every client (pi, herdr workers, opencode-go) to implement the sync.
- **Option B (pragmatic, server-only):** after a live compaction record `session.compacted_from_count`. On the next request, if `history_mismatch` AND the incoming messages are consistent with "client still has pre-compaction history" (same recent turns + new tail), accept the delta against the compacted base instead of invalidating. Clear the marker after one use. Matches the existing fail-open philosophy.

### Part 3 — Collapse the three detection paths
Single knob: `compaction_trigger_ratio`. At trigger, log the advisory AND arm the live path (or the 429 gate if the summarizer is unavailable). Remove `context_pressure_warn_ratio` and `local_hard_routing_cap_ratio_cheap` as separate knobs. Do this after the live path is proven by Parts 1–2.

### Part 4 — Client-side compaction sync (later)
- **Investigation first:** study how Pi handles compaction internally — Pi frequently compacts on the client side already (emitting "The conversation history before this point was compacted into the following summary" blocks). Understand its summary envelope, trigger conditions, and whether/how it re-syncs history with the server (full-history re-send vs delta, marker format, any existing headers it respects). The server-side design must interoperate with — not fight — Pi's client-side compaction.
- Then design the long-term client adoption path (Part 2 Option A): server `X-Session-Compacted` headers + client re-sync, aligned with Pi's existing compaction envelope so double-compaction (client summarizes, then server re-summarizes the summary) is avoided.
- Retire the Part 2 Option B tolerance once clients adopt the sync.

# Server-side auto-recovery for post-content stalls (Fix A)

## Problem

When Muse stalls mid-stream *after* content has been delivered, the proxy emits a terminal `stall_after_content` error chunk and **never retries** (LP-0MS9FR9LG002AJ4C design). The client (Pi/herdr) sees a hard error and requires manual `continue`. This is a dead end because:

1. The fallback chain never activates (terminal error chunks bypass `StreamingPreContentError` handling)
2. All 3 opencode-go entries share a failure domain, so no sibling is available
3. DeepSeek may be unavailable (gated by `available_times`)
4. The parent RCA (LP-0MTV77DAT0018ZUS) identifies this as the dominant stall pattern (8 observed in a single day)

## Goal

Enable the proxy to automatically re-dispatch stalled post-content requests to the next healthy provider in the chain, without requiring manual `continue` input from the operator.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Auto-recovery on stall_after_content:** When the proxy detects a post-content stall (`_terminate_after_content = True`), instead of yielding a terminal error chunk, it buffers the partial content and raises a `StreamingRecoverableAfterContentError` (new exception type, sibling to `StreamingPreContentError` and `StreamingRecoverableAfterReasoningError`)

2. **AC2 — Fallback chain activation:** The fallback chain (`provider.py`) catches `StreamingRecoverableAfterContentError`, discards the partial content prefix, and re-dispatches to the next healthy provider using the full request context

3. **AC3 — Idempotency guard:** If the upstream somehow processes both the original and re-dispatched request, the client receives a complete answer from the fallback provider and can safely discard the partial prefix. No duplicate tool calls reach the client.

4. **AC4 — Observability:** Auto-recovery events are logged with `suggested_action`, and a new metric `llama_remote_stream_recovered_total{reason=\"stall_after_content\"}` is incremented for observability

5. **AC5 — No regression on tool-call-only stalls:** If the stall occurs after tool_calls were delivered (but no final content), the behavior is unchanged — the enriched error event reaches the client (existing behavior preserved per operator decision Q1)

6. **AC6 — Config flag:** Add `server.auto_recovery_stall_after_content: true` (default `true`) for opt-out if needed

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1: Add new exception type (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`)

```python
class StreamingRecoverableAfterContentError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, provider_name, message, partial_content: bytes = b""):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.provider_name = provider_name
        self.partial_content = partial_content
```

### Step 2: Modify stall handling (`proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py`)

In `_handle_remote_streaming`, when `_terminate_after_content` is set, check the config flag and raise the new exception instead of yielding terminal error:

```python
if _terminate_after_content:
    auto_recovery = _srv().config.get("server", {}).get("auto_recovery_stall_after_content", True)
    if auto_recovery:
        raise StreamingRecoverableAfterContentError(provider, "stall_after_content", partial_content=...)
    yield _final_error_bytes
    break
```

### Step 3: Handle in fallback chain (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`)

Add handler alongside existing `StreamingPreContentError` handlers in both streaming paths:

```python
except StreamingRecoverableAfterContentError as exc:
    mark_provider_unavailable(provider_name, cooldown_seconds)
    _record_sibling_failure(provider_name, config, provider_cfg.get("provider"))
    attempted_domains.add(_failure_domain_key(provider_cfg))
    # Log + metric, then continue to next provider
    fallback_reason = "stall_after_content_recoverable"
    continue
```

### Step 4: Add config key (`proxy/config.yaml`)

```yaml
server:
  auto_recovery_stall_after_content: true
```

### Step 5: Add metric tracking

Prometheus counter `llama_remote_stream_recovered_total` with labels reason/from_provider/to_provider.

## Risks

- **Partial content already sent to client:** The partial prefix has already reached the client. Recovery must discard it (client sees brief glitch then fresh stream).
- **Duplicate billing:** If both original and re-dispatched request reach upstream. Mitigation: proxy discards partial, fallback generates fresh answer.
- **Stall propagation:** If upstream is genuinely unhealthy, recovery lands on another stall. Mitigation: existing Tier-3 circuit breaker and failure-domain grouping still apply.

## Related

- RCA: LP-0MTV77DAT0018ZUS (Fix A)
- LP-0MS9FR9LG002AJ4C — `_terminate_after_content` design (the cause)
- LP-0MSF1PUM90099ZSW — Mid-stream stall fallback (completed, pre-content only)
- LP-0MSDRRDWK009QT4E — Silent continue for pre-content failures (completed)
- LP-0MTPMF03P0046MFG — Sibling provider switching (completed)
- LP-0MRFEXXVC001RYKB — Stall circuit breaker (Tier-3)
- LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F — Failure domain grouping
data.title: Server-side auto-recovery for post-content stalls (Fix A)

# Feature: Dedicated small summarizer model for proxy-side session compaction

## Problem

Observed 2026-09-11 ~20:14-20:15: the proxy's local summarizer timed out 3x over ~1 minute during a live session compaction (session 01a091ac). The summarizer call shares the main Qwen3.6-35B-A3B slots with all active Pi/herdr sessions, so it competes for decode bandwidth with active sessions. When those sessions are busy (e.g. long reasoning traces), the summarizer times out and the proxy falls back to 'fast' mode compaction (less thorough) — degrading compaction quality.

Evidence from proxy log:
- 20:14:18 local summarizer transport error (attempt 1/3): timed out
- 20:14:48 local summarizer transport error (attempt 2/3): timed out
- 20:15:19 local summarizer call failed after 3 attempts: timed out
- 20:15:19 compaction_event mode=fast (fallback, not summarize-then-compact)

## Proposed solution

Load a small, dedicated summarizer model (e.g. Qwen 7-8B class) in the llama.cpp router with a single slot, rewired as the summarizer model for proxy-side compaction. VRAM is not a constraint (120GB ROCm GPU, ~30GB currently used, ~90GB headroom).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Best summarizer model selected and documented (compare candidates on: summarization quality for session history, VRAM footprint, latency when main model is under load; document decision and rationale)
2. New small model added to models.ini with its own router slot (parallel=1), loaded alongside Qwen3 without disrupting existing sessions
3. Proxy compaction config (summarizer_model, see LP-0MTG6RW3L003X122) points at the new dedicated model instead of reusing Qwen3
4. Under load, summarizer calls complete without the 3x-timeout pattern observed above (verify via proxy log: no 'local summarizer transport error' in a 24h window post-change)
5. Compaction quality at least as good as before: mode=fast fallback rate does not increase; summarize-driven compactions succeed
6. Existing test suites pass

## Notes

- VRAM headroom confirmed (~90GB free on the 120GB AMD gfx1151); an 8B Q4 model is ~4-5GB — negligible
- Single-GPU bandwidth contention remains: if the main model is saturated during compaction windows the small model still shares the memory bus. Dedicated slot buys availability (no queue wait), not raw throughput. CPU offloading or a second GPU are longer-term options if timeouts persist
- Depends on: LP-0MTG6RW3L003X122-derived fallback-model work — if a summarizer-fallback-model work item does not yet exist, create it and record a blocking dependency on it

## Problem

Session 01a091ac (fast mode) compacted cleanly — 63,282 → 35,567 tokens, `compacted_within_target`, live mode (`dry_run=False`) — yet dispatch fell through to `opencode-go-2` (muse-spark) with `reason=HTTP 400` from local-qwen3. Compaction's size reduction never got a chance to matter because the local backend rejected the compacted request before routing could succeed locally.

Evidence (2026-09-11 20:23 UTC, /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log):

```
compaction_event session=01a091ac mode=fast action=compact
  reason=compacted_within_target pre_tokens=63282 post_tokens=35567
  turns_summarized=2 turns_dropped=0 dry_run=False
session_compaction applied session=01a091ac est_before=63282 est_after=35567
routing_estimate_session session=01a091ac request_tokens=35567 session_tokens=63282
Fallback triggered for model=v1/chat/completions,
  from=local-qwen3, to=opencode-go-2, reason=HTTP 400
```

A session compacted within target dispatches locally instead of silently falling through on a local 400.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Root cause identified:** the 400's source is confirmed (reasoning_content round-trip vs compacted-prefix/slot mismatch) via the upstream body snippet for a reproduced compacted-history request.
2. **AC2 — No silent fallthrough on this class:** a local 400 that is deterministic for the session (repeats turn after turn on the same history) escalates visibly (log WARNING + metric) rather than silently routing remote each turn.
3. **AC3 — Compaction→local path works:** a session compacted within target routes local on the next turn (verify `Stream started: provider=local` after `session_compaction applied` with est_after under target).

# Server-side compaction not durable across turns: force_full_prompt discards the compacted base

## Problem

Server-side compaction rewrites the dispatch body on the turn it fires, but the compacted history is not the dispatch base on subsequent turns. The client (Pi) re-sends its own full, uncompacted history every request, and the proxy both (a) refuses delta routing because `force_full_prompt` is set, and (b) replaces the session store with the client's full request messages. Net effect: compaction only ever benefits the single turn it fires on, and the session returns to its uncompacted size immediately — so compaction cannot bring an oversized session back to local.

## Evidence (code)

`proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_classify_delta_routing`:

```python
if force_full_prompt:
    logger.info("cache_invalidation: full re-process required - delta_disabled (force_full_prompt=True)")
    return False, "delta_disabled"
```

`proxy/proxy/session.py` — `merge_session_history_for_update`:

```python
if is_delta_request and delta_messages:
    merged = list(existing_messages) + list(delta_messages)
else:
    merged = list(request_messages)          # client's full, uncompacted history
```

`force_full_prompt: true` is set on all three models in all three configs: `proxy/config.yaml:271,339,405`, `proxy/config-cheap.yaml:271,339,405`, `proxy/config-fast.yaml:246,314,380`.

## Evidence (runtime)

Session `01a091ac`, `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`:

```
20:23:11 compaction_event ... pre_tokens=63282 post_tokens=35567 dry_run=False
20:23:11 session_compaction applied ... est_before=63282 est_after=35567
20:23:15 routing_check estimated_tokens=79419 messages=72      ← next request already bigger than the compacted size
20:23:15 Session ... history match=True delta_messages=22 using full prompt reason=delta_disabled
20:23:30 compaction_event ... pre_tokens=63282 post_tokens=35567  ← identical to the previous event
```

8 live events, all byte-identical (`pre=63282 post=35567`), then compaction stopped firing entirely while context grew 63K → 112K; the session now skips local every turn with `routing_skip_local reason=context_too_large` (ratio 1.35 vs per-slot 83,285).

## Goal

A compacted session dispatches `compacted_history + the client's new turns`, so the compaction reduction persists across turns and keeps the session within the local per-slot budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Compaction is durable:** for a session compacted on turn N, the dispatch base on turn N+1 is the compacted history plus only the client's new turns — not the client's full history. Verified by test and by `routing_estimate_session` showing the post-compaction size on the following turn.
2. **AC2 — Estimates agree:** `routing_check` / `routing_estimate_session` for a compacted session report the compacted size, not a pre-compaction or stale value.
3. **AC3 — Session store consistency:** the session store holds the compacted base (or the compacted base plus new turns) after a compaction turn, and is not overwritten by the client's full body.
4. **AC4 — Oversized session recovers to local:** a session that was routed remote solely because it exceeded the per-slot cap returns to local on a subsequent turn after compaction brings it under the cap.
5. **AC5 — KV/slot correctness:** the compacted prefix is the prefix used for slot save/restore; no stale-prefix reuse produces incorrect output.
6. **AC6 — No regression:** sessions that are not compacted continue to behave exactly as today (full-prompt dispatch where `force_full_prompt` is set).
7. **AC7 — Documentation updated:** the dispatch-base contract (client history vs compacted session history) is documented in the compaction/session docs and code comments.
8. **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- `force_full_prompt` was presumably set because slot/KV restore is not reliably confirmed for the local backend; relaxing `delta_disabled` for compacted sessions must not cause stale-prefix reuse. The compacted base must be the prefix actually resident/restorable in the slot.
- Do not implement before the dispatch-base contract is agreed (this is an architectural change to prompt assembly).
- Depends on the summarizer fail-open fix: making compaction durable while summaries are empty would amplify content loss.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_classify_delta_routing`, `merge_session_history_for_update`, `compute_delta`.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_handle_session`, `_evaluate_session_compaction`, `_should_force_full_prompt_from_config`.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `_update_session_and_slot`, hard routing cap gate.
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py` — `plan_session_compaction`, `decide_session_compaction`.
- `proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/config-fast.yaml`, `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — `force_full_prompt`.

## Related

- RCA: LP-0MTV77DAT0018ZUS
- LP-0MTWTUOXH008TFME — enabled live compaction (config flip)
- LP-0MTXEBQ4E001BMI2 — local HTTP 400 on compacted history forces silent remote fallthrough
- LP-0MTXEED8E003EDM8 — `routing_estimate_session` reports pre-compaction `session_tokens`
- Sibling: summarizer fail-open returns empty summary
- Sibling: Pi client compaction never fires

# Pi client compaction never fires: Local Proxy models declare no contextWindow

## Problem

Pi (the client) auto-compacts its own history when `contextTokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens`. For the `Local Proxy` provider the models are declared with bare IDs and no `contextWindow`, so Pi falls back to its built-in default of 128,000. The resulting threshold is 111,616 tokens — but no `CompactionEntry` has been written for any session since 2026-09-09, even though sessions have run well past that threshold. Because Pi's history is the authoritative one for dispatch (the proxy dispatches the client's full body — see the sibling item on `force_full_prompt`), Pi compaction is the only mechanism that durably shrinks a request. It not firing means oversized sessions never recover.

## Evidence

`~/.pi/agent/models.json` — no `contextWindow` or `maxTokens` for any Local Proxy model:

```json
"Local Proxy": {
  "api": "openai-completions",
  "baseUrl": "http://192.168.0.199:8000/v1",
  "models": [ { "id": "plan" }, { "id": "code" }, { "id": "author" }, { "id": "qwen3" }, { "id": "gpt120" } ]
}
```

Pi's fallback (`dist/core/provider-composer.js:72`):

```js
contextWindow: definition.contextWindow ?? 128000,
```

With `reserveTokens: 16384` (no `compaction` block in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, so defaults apply), Pi's threshold is **111,616**.

Yet the 8 most recent `CompactionEntry` records across every session in every project under `~/.pi/agent/sessions` are:

```
2026-09-09T22:27  tokensBefore=111802
2026-09-09T17:03  tokensBefore=117527
2026-09-09T16:57  tokensBefore=113614
2026-08-13 ×5     tokensBefore=111632 … 290588
```

Nothing on 2026-09-10 or 2026-09-11. Meanwhile session `01a091ac`'s own Pi usage records show `cacheRead` climbing to **173,824** with `totalTokens` **175,989** — far above 111,616 — and still no compaction entry.

Working Pi version: `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` **0.85.1** (compaction entry type is `"compaction"`, same as the older `@mariozechner` package).

## Goal

Pi compacts its own history at an appropriate threshold for the `Local Proxy` models, so oversized sessions shrink client-side and return to local dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Correct context window:** the `Local Proxy` models declare the real context window (and `maxTokens` where relevant) in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`, so Pi's computed compaction threshold matches the model's actual capacity.
2. **AC2 — Compaction observed:** a session that exceeds the threshold produces a `CompactionEntry` (`{"type":"compaction", summary, firstKeptEntryId, tokensBefore}`) in its Pi session JSONL.

# Instrument session store and compaction dispatch base to resolve frozen pre_tokens anomaly

## Problem

While investigating why server-side compaction does not return an oversized session to local, an anomaly emerged that the current logs cannot explain. Session `01a091ac` produced 8 live compaction events over ~18 minutes (20:12–20:30) with **byte-identical** figures:

```
pre_tokens=63282 post_tokens=35567 turns_summarized=2 turns_dropped=0 summary_tokens=0 dry_run=False
```

If the session store were being replaced each turn by the client's growing full history (as `merge_session_history_for_update` implies for a non-delta request), `pre_tokens` should have grown turn over turn. It did not — and after 20:30:57 compaction stopped firing entirely while context grew 63K → 112K with no further `compaction_event` lines, and no `Session 01a091ac...` / `Session header resolved` lines at all.

Without knowing what `session.messages` actually contained, and which base compaction evaluated versus which base was dispatched, we cannot design the durability fix correctly. This item produces that evidence; it is a prerequisite for the sibling architectural fix.

## Goal

Produce a definitive, evidence-backed description of what the session store holds and which message list each decision consumes, across a compaction turn and the turn that follows it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Instrumented decision trail:** for each request in a target session, log (at INFO/DEBUG, session-scoped) the values needed to explain the decision: `len(session.messages)` and its token estimate, `len(body_json["messages"])` and its token estimate, the compaction trigger/target, the chosen action, whether `body_override` was applied, and whether the session was created/invalidated/`history_mismatch`.
2. **AC2 — Turn-over-turn capture:** capture a compacted turn and the immediately following turn, showing exactly why `pre_tokens` did or did not change, and why compaction stopped firing after 20:30:57 (`Session header resolved` also stopped appearing for that session — determine which branch `_handle_session` took).
3. **AC3 — Documented answer:** a written finding (work-item comment or linked doc) states authoritatively: (a) what the session store contains after a compaction turn and after the next turn; (b) why `pre_tokens` was frozen; (c) why compaction stopped firing; (d) which code path replaces or preserves the compacted history.
4. **AC4 — Feeds the durability design:** the finding lists the exact code changes required for the sibling durability fix, or identifies a different root cause than the assumed `force_full_prompt` / non-delta-replacement mechanism.
5. **AC5 — Instrumentation is safe:** added logging is low-volume (no per-token or per-message spam), does not change dispatch behaviour, and is either removed or left at DEBUG behind the existing logging configuration.
6. **AC6 — Documentation updated:** findings recorded wherever the compaction/session architecture is documented.
7. **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_handle_session`, `_evaluate_session_compaction`, `_should_force_full_prompt_from_config` (the compaction evaluation and its inputs).
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `_update_session_and_slot` (post-response persistence), hard routing-cap gate.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `merge_session_history_for_update`, `compute_delta`, `_classify_delta_routing`, `_invalidate_session_and_slot`.
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py` — `plan_session_compaction` (estimates and trigger).

# Per-model compaction trigger configuration

## Problem Statement

The proxy-side compaction trigger (`compaction_trigger_ratio: 0.70`) is a single global value in `server.*` config. It applies uniformly to all models, regardless of their context window size or expected session length. Different models may benefit from different trigger ratios — e.g., a smaller-context model might need a lower ratio to compact earlier, while a larger-context model could tolerate a higher ratio.

The trigger formula is:
```
estimated_tokens > trigger_ratio × effective_per_slot_threshold(ctx_size, slots)
```

Currently `trigger_ratio` is the same for every model. This means a 64K model and a 256K model both fire compaction at 70% of their respective per-slot thresholds — which may not be optimal for either.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Per-model compaction config supported:** Each model entry in `config.yaml` may include an optional `compaction` section with keys `trigger_ratio`, `summarizer_ctx_size`, and `summarizer_max_tokens`. When present, these override the global `server.compaction_*` defaults for that model.
2. **AC2 — Global defaults preserved:** When a model entry omits the `compaction` section, the global `server.compaction_*` values apply unchanged (zero behavior change for existing configs).
3. **AC3 — Config is documented:** `proxy/config.yaml` documents the new per-model `compaction` block alongside the existing global config.
4. **AC4 — Tests updated:** Tests for `compaction_config()` in `provider.py` cover the per-model override path and the global-default fallback.

## Important Note: Client-Side Compaction

**This change should only be carried out if the client is honouring server-side compaction.** The proxy-side compaction currently operates with `compaction_dry_run: true`, meaning it is in advisory mode only — it does not actually rewrite dispatch bodies. Until the client honours the server-side compaction signal (i.e., the client actually compacts its own history in response to server guidance, or the proxy enforces compaction in live mode), a per-model trigger configuration would add complexity without realising the benefit of earlier/late compaction.

In other words: the per-model configuration is a precision tuning of a mechanism that is currently disabled. Prioritise getting server-side compaction live (flip `compaction_dry_run: false`) and verifying client-side compliance before investing in per-model knobs.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `compaction_config()` (resolve per-model overrides)
- `proxy/config.yaml` — model-level `compaction` section
- `proxy/tests/` — tests for the new config resolution path

## Bug: proxy-usage-analysis discovers only dot-named rotated logs; logrotate's dash-named daily files (daytime traffic) are silently dropped

### Problem Statement

`discover_log_files` in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` (line 573) only accepts
`p.name == "proxy.log"` or `p.name.startswith("proxy.log.")` (dot scheme). The deployment has **two** rotation
mechanisms writing the same log stream:

| Mechanism | Naming | File in /var/log/llama-proxy | Content span (2026-09-11) |
|---|---|---|---|
| In-process TimedRotatingFileHandler (proxy/utils.py, 6h) | `proxy.log.YYYY-MM-DD_HH` | `proxy.log.2026-09-11_01.gz` | 00:00:10 → 07:00:33 (overnight) |
| logrotate safety net (/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy, daily copytruncate, `dateformat -%Y-%m-%d_%H`) | `proxy.log-YYYY-MM-DD_HH` | `proxy.log-2026-09-12_00` (4.8 MB) | 07:00:46 → 23:59:55 (**all daytime**) |

The two schemes are empirically contiguous and non-overlapping: the dash file carries 07:00→23:59 of each day,
the dot file 00:00→07:00. `discover_log_files` matches only the dot form, so **every dash file — including the
largest single file, the one holding the whole daytime — is excluded silently**. For a 24h window this makes most
daytime hours appear empty, which is exactly the symptom that triggered this investigation
("report shows long periods of nothing being scheduled while the proxy was busy all day").

### Observed impact (same 24h window, 2026-09-11 11:04 → 2026-09-12 11:04)

| Metric | Without dash files (current code: 14 files) | With dash files (22 files) |
|---|---|---|
| Files scanned | 14 | 22 |
| Sessions | 23 | 52–55 |
| Requests | 480 | 1585–1642 |
| Local busy | 6.2% (5353 s) | 22.9% (19760 s) |
| Fallbacks | 87 (18.1%) | 740 (45.1%) |
| Errors | 24 | 112–116 |

Regresses AC2 of completed work item `LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR` ("discover_log_files never excludes a rotated file
that overlaps the analysis window"). The dash files are a documented part of the deployment (installed by
HOST_INSTALL.md step 6).

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A 24h analysis window includes data from dash-named files (e.g. `proxy.log-2026-09-12_00`): for window
   `2026-09-11 11:04 → 2026-09-12 11:04`, reports >= 22 files scanned and busy time >= 20% (true value ~22.9%).
2. `discover_log_files` never excludes a rotated proxy-log file (dot or dash) whose content overlaps the window,
   with no double counting if the two schemes ever overlap in content.
3. `iter_events` per-line timestamp filtering remains the authoritative boundary check (no change to that logic).
4. New regression tests cover both naming schemes (dot + dash, gz + plain), sorted output, and a window that
   straddles a dash file boundary.
5. Existing suite in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` passes (263 tests).
6. Fix is implemented via the standard worktree workflow (implement skill), not the main checkout.

## Bug: local dispatch pool permanently wedged by leaked local_generating_queries/local_generating_sessions — no self-healing exists; only a proxy restart recovers

### Problem Statement

On 2026-09-11 11:55 the local model went dark for 2h 11m (11:55:11 → 14:06:50) while the proxy was otherwise
fully busy (155 streams served in 12:00–18:00, all but 2 via remote fallback). Every local dispatch attempt in
that window was refused with `local_dispatch_denied session=<s> owner=none active=3` even though **zero** local
streams were in flight and the dispatch lease table was empty (`owner=none` at 12:09:46 onwards). Only a process
restart (14:07:03) restored local service (local streams resumed at 14:06:50).

### Evidence (from /var/log/llama-proxy, window 2026-09-11 11:00 → 12:00)

- 11:55:11,792 — last local `Stream finished` before the gap (session 01a08fa5-…; also herdr-1789116877 at 11:55:11,778, herdr-1789116084 at 11:53:39).
- 12:06:43 … 12:56:50 — 30 `local_dispatch_denied … owner=none active=3` events; zero `Stream started: provider=local` until 14:06:50.
- 12:08:14 — `active_queries counter recovered: reset from 1 to 0` (self-healing fired) yet denials continue with `owner=none` → lease table empty, pool still reported full.
- 14:07:03 — new process started (dispatch lease cleanup task), local works again.

### Root cause

`_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py ~1355) checks `_generating_count` =
`len(local_generating_queries)` first (with `_prefill_count` guard second). `local_generating_queries` /
`local_generating_sessions` are maintained per-session (idempotent set) by `_increment_generating_only_slot`
(router_helpers.py ~1154) and `_decrement_generating_only_slot` (~1205). The decrement runs only at
proxy/proxy/router.py:1788 inside the streaming generator's `finally` block, AFTER unguarded
`slot_lock_coordinator.acquire(slot_id)` / `await _update_session_and_slot(...)` (router.py ~1699–1713): an
exception there (slot lock timeout, upstream httpx failure) aborts the rest of the `finally`, so the decrement
and `_cleanup_after_request` never run and the session key leaks into `local_generating_sessions` forever.

The 10-second `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` (proxy/proxy/server.py ~199–213) self-heals `local_active_queries`
(`_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch`, `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries`) and the global `active_queries`
(`_recover_stuck_global_active_queries`), and pops `local_prefill_in_flight` — but **nothing ever reclaims
`local_generating_queries` / `local_generating_sessions`**. When the count leaks to max_local (3), the pool is
permanently blocked for everyone until a process restart.

Corroboration:
- The 3 sessions denied immediately after the gap (01a08fa5-8288-77ea-9d53-262e87528e47, herdr-1789116084-477525-6502, herdr-1789116877-466048-28018) are exactly the 3 sessions with the last local streams before 11:55, and exactly max_local (=3, --parallel 3, slot scheduler 10:00→3).
- The leak coincides with a llama-server stress window (11:44–11:55: repeated context_too_large / large_context_bypass finishes, slot_busy persistence skips, summarizer timeouts).
- Report impact: `local_concurrency_limit` is the single largest fallback reason in the 24h report — 294 events (39.7% of 740), i.e. this class of failure dominates fallback behaviour.
- Codebase precedent: LP-0MRIL2L3E0080OGC "Harden _decrement_local_active_queries against silent counter leaks"; LP-0MQTHOPS10066BFJ removed yield-in-finally to make cleanup reachable — but the unguarded calls still allow aborts.

### Secondary local-idle cause (same day, 14:06:54 → 18:24:24)

After the restart, local was skipped by routing policy instead: 115 `routing_skip_local reason=context_too_large`
+ 19 `large_context_bypass` (sessions' contexts grew to 101k–117k tokens; compaction had been failing at
12:00–12:08 with `local summarizer transport error (attempt 1/3): timed out`). Skipped-by-policy requests never
produce a `[local] POST` line, so hour 13 shows zero local attempts. This is a capacity-tuning issue, not a
counter leak, but should be monitored alongside this fix.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Reproduce: with max_local=3, force a scenario where a stream generator's finally block aborts after
   incrementing the generating counter; verify the pool is blocked afterwards.
2. `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` reclaims stale `local_generating_queries` / `local_generating_sessions` entries
   (or the streaming generator's cleanup is made non-skippable, e.g. the slot-save/`_update_session_and_slot`
   calls are guarded with try/finally so the decrement always runs on any exit path, including CancelledError).
3. After recovery, `local_dispatch_denied … owner=none active=3` with zero in-flight local streams can no longer
   persist; pool self-heals within a bounded interval (e.g. two cleanup ticks) without a restart.
4. Regression unit tests: (a) leak of N session keys then cleanup tick reclaims them; (b) exception inside the
   finally's slot-save path still decrements the generating counter; (c) max_local block clears without restart.
5. Existing proxy test suite passes.
6. Implemented via the standard worktree workflow (implement skill), not the main checkout.

### Notes / related

- LP-0MTED3OLC001RJN4 investigated a similar idle-time `local_concurrency_limit` symptom on the
  `local_active_queries` side (completed) — this leak is on the generating-only counter introduced by
  LP-0MTJET5IP004TD6K / LP-0MTH7JX82000YS5N.

## Bug: proxy-usage-analysis hourly table hides real activity — session-first-hour attribution, no per-hour traffic columns, and duplicate hour-of-day buckets yield impossible >100% rows

### Problem Statement

The "Summary by hour" table in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` has three defects that together make hours
with heavy traffic look empty and produce nonsensical rows:

1. **Session-first-hour attribution only.** The three classification columns
   (`Started local, completed local` / `Started local, fell back` / `Started remote-only`) count sessions by the
   hour of their **first request**, not their activity. A session that starts at 09:00 and runs until 12:00
   contributes nothing to the 10:00/11:00 rows. There are no per-hour Request / Fallback / Local-attempt /
   Local-skip columns, so remote-and-fallback-heavy hours report all zeros.

   Observed on 2026-09-11: the table shows `12:00–18:00` as essentially empty (one session row at 12:00, one at
   14:00) while the proxy actually served **155 streams** in that span (153 opencode-go + 2 local) and logged
   **134 routing_skip_local (context_too_large) decisions** and ~300 fallbacks.

2. **Duplicate hour-of-day bucket rows (rolling windows).** For a 24h window starting at 11:04 the table emits
   both a 56-minute `11:04-12:00` row and a 4-minute `11:00-11:04` row. Both are keyed by the same hour-of-day
   bucket, so the same busy duration is written to both and the 4-minute denominator yields an impossible row:
   `| 11:00-11:04 | 15m 10s | 305.3% |`. The totals row stays correct (merged unions), masking the defect.

3. **Busy% denominator is window-bounded per row** (partial rows), which combined with (2) produces >100%
   display values rather than being clamped or merged.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Hourly table includes per-hour columns that reflect activity attributable to the hour: e.g. requests started,
   local-attempts, local-served, fallbacks, local-skip decisions — counted by event timestamp, not session-start
   hour.
2. Rolling-window runs never emit two rows for the same hour-of-day; no row shows a busy% > 100% or a busy
   duration that duplicates another row.
3. For window `2026-09-11 11:04 → 2026-09-12 11:04`, the 12:00–18:00 rows show non-zero activity (>= 155
   streams attributable across those hours).
4. Existing suite in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` passes; new tests cover the rolling-window
   duplicate-bucket case and the per-hour attribution.
5. Implemented via the standard worktree workflow (implement skill), not the main checkout.

### Context

- The 305.3% artifact was verified present in the latest report (archived `2026-09-12_5`): last table row
  `| 11:00-11:04 | 15m 10s | 305.3% | … | 5 (100.0%) |`.
- Related completed items: LP-0MTFO210Q0044TTF (per-hour request-start classification columns), LP-0MSVMLM7G009N74N (retitle/bound hours) — this item fixes the attribution and bucketing defects those introduced.

# Surface proxy-side compaction metadata in responses (Pi client bridge)

Enable the Pi coding-agent client to keep its dispatched view consistent
with the proxy's compacted session history, without client modifications.
Today the proxy compacts server-side (parent LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD machinery)
but the compaction decision and the injected summary marker are invisible
to the client: Pi keeps sending its full un-compacted history, which
forces history_mismatch fallbacks and CREATION re-summarization on every
turn (churn). This item adds the wire signal; the client-side consumer
lives in the SorraAgents project (Pi extension work item, cross-
referenced in Notes).

## User Story

As a Pi client user, I want the proxy to tell me when it compacted my
session and what the compacted view looks like, so my client can dispatch
the same compacted history and the proxy can resume incremental
(summarize-first) compaction instead of re-summarizing from scratch.

## Design

Flow:

    Turn N:  proxy compacts session history to
               [system, first_user, summary_marker, recent...]
             sets response headers:
               X-Compaction-Occurred: true
               X-Compaction-Marker: <base64 of exact marker content>
               X-Compaction-Turns-Summarized: <n>
               X-Compaction-Recent-Turns-Kept: <n>
    Client extension (SorraAgents) reads headers, mirrors the view in
    its dispatch layer on the next turn (JSONL storage untouched).

Changes:

1. `proxy/router_helpers.py` `_handle_session`: when compaction is applied
   (`result["compaction_applied"] = True`), additionally surface
   `compaction_summary_text`, `compaction_turns_summarized`,
   `compaction_recent_turns_kept` on the session result, taken from the
   `decide_session_compaction` plan dict (`_compaction`).
2. `proxy/router.py`: after `outgoing_headers` is assembled (near the
   `X-Resolved-Model` header), when compaction was applied, add the four
   headers. The marker is built from the proxy's exact
   `_SUMMARY_MARKER` / `_SUMMARY_MARKER_END` delimiters
   (`compaction.py`) so the client never has to replicate the marker
   format (no drift).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When live compaction is applied for a request, the response
  includes `X-Compaction-Occurred: true` plus `X-Compaction-Marker`,
  `X-Compaction-Turns-Summarized`, `X-Compaction-Recent-Turns-Kept`.
- AC2: The marker header content decodes to the exact message content
  the proxy injected into the compacted history (verbatim, including
  delimiters).
- AC3: Non-compaction responses (noop / below-trigger / dry-run /
  remote_with_guidance) set none of these headers.
- AC4: Header emission is fail-safe: any error surfaces no compaction
  headers and never changes dispatch behaviour — the header block is
  additive only, after compaction has already been applied.
- AC5: Headers survive streaming responses (SSE) — set on the outgoing
  `StreamingResponse`, not inside the streamed body.
- AC6: Unit tests cover the header contract: applied-compaction,
  dry-run, noop, remote_with_guidance, and marker round-trip
  (encode → decode → equals injected message content).

## Notes / related

- Companion work item (client extension): SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0 in the
  SorraAgents project.
- Reuses the existing compaction plan fields (`summary_text`,
  `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`) already returned by
  `plan_session_compaction` — no changes to compaction logic itself.
- Header size caveat: summaries are base64'd into one header; if real
  summaries exceed a few KB, revisit with a sidecar endpoint
  (`GET /sessions/<id>/compaction`).
data.title: Surface proxy-side compaction metadata in responses (Pi client bridge)
